PCAP packet iteration and write helpers for Ethernet, cooked SLL, VLAN, IP, and UDP frames.

# Purpose
This file implements PCAP file support for packet capture and packet generation. It defines the PCAP file header and packet record formats, then provides iterator functions to read packets from a `FILE` stream, including support for Ethernet captures and Linux cooked socket captures (`FD_PCAP_HDR_NETWORK_LINUX_SLL`). The read path validates the PCAP magic number, checks the link-layer type, reads each packet header, and copies packet data into caller buffers. It also handles VLAN tags, IPv4 headers, IPv4 options, and UDP headers when the caller uses the split-header read function [`fd_pcap_iter_next_split`](<#fd_pcap_iter_next_split>).

The file also provides write helpers for PCAP output. Functions such as [`fd_pcap_fwrite_hdr`](<#fd_pcap_fwrite_hdr>), [`fd_pcap_ostream_hdr`](<#fd_pcap_ostream_hdr>), [`fd_pcap_pkt`](<#fd_pcap_pkt>), [`fd_pcap_fwrite_pkt`](<#fd_pcap_fwrite_pkt>), and [`fd_pcap_ostream_pkt`](<#fd_pcap_ostream_pkt>) build a PCAP global header and packet records for either standard `FILE` output or buffered stream output. The packet write code stores timestamps, lengths, header bytes, payload bytes, and a final FCS field. The code is compiled only when `FD_HAS_HOSTED` is set, so it is intended for hosted targets that can use standard I/O.
